Calculation of Radial Rigidity
Stiffness and Preload for Sets

factor in the table  to
the left. To derive the
radial stiffness for three or four bearings in a set, i.e. if the
catalogue axial rigidity was 200N/μm for 15°, Light preload; the
radial rigidity for a set of 3 would be 200x6x1.54 = 1848N/μm.
3. Useful Tip
In an emergency situation, if the correct preloaded bearing is not
available and spacers are used, it is possible to use a different
preload set of bearings and adjust the spacers to compensate.
The NSK Super Precision catalogue shows the axial clearances
for each set of angular contact bearings,
Example:
If a 7906CTRDUHP4 is required but only 7906CTRDUMP4 is
available, the spacer can be machined to compensate for the
different preload. From the table above for 30mm bore the Heavy
preload axial clearance is 16μm and the Medium preload axial
clearance is 9μm. therefore to change from Medium preload to
Heavy preload it is necessary to change the spacer length by the
difference i.e. 16μm – 9μm = 7μm. In this case because we are
increasing the preload we need to reduce the inner ring spacer
by 7μm and leave the outer spacer untouched.
This information has been extracted from the Global catalogue or
can be found on pages 65 to 67 for your reference.
Rule:
To increase preload: reduce inner ring spacer
To reduce preload: reduce outer ring spacer
Remember: this is for emergency situations only, if the preload
is changed in this way care should be taken to document the
changes so that if the bearings are replaced in the future the
correct preload is selected to allow for the spacer changes.
Spacers
In the example of
three rows, it can be
seen that the internal
preload is not shared
evenly, this means
that one bearing is
taking twice the preload of the pair and will operate at a
slightly higher temperature. For this reason, it can be seen
from the  Speed factors table (page 14), that the speed
capability of a set of three is less than a set of four.
Load can be applied from either direction but greater load
from the left side.
The NSK Super Precision catalogue also states the preload and
axial rigidity for pairs of all products. This information is useful
when testing a newly assembled spindle. The radial rigidity can
be simply calculated by using the factors in the table below
i.e. for Light preload and 15° contact angle, multiply axial
stiffness given in the catalogue by 6 to get the radial stiffness.

system.text:
You transcribe the parts of an equipment-documentation page that its text layer cannot carry: tables (with their rows and columns), figures (screenshots, photos, diagrams, charts, drawings) and, when the text layer is empty or unreadable, the page text itself.

You get the page as an image and its text layer as extracted from the PDF. The text layer is kept as it is; do not repeat body paragraphs from it.

Tables:
- Report every table on the page, including tables without ruling lines and tables that are part of an image.
- One row per printed row, cells in column order. Copy each cell exactly as printed: keep decimal commas, units, signs, dashes and symbols. Use '' for an empty cell.
- Merged cells: a value printed once for a group of rows (often centred vertically on the group, or standing beside a brace or between two horizontal rules) belongs to every row in that group. Write it in every row it spans, never only in the row it happens to sit next to, and never leave the other rows ''. The same holds for a heading or value spanning several columns.
- Put column headings in `header`. A heading printed on two lines is one heading.
- `source` is text_layer if the cell texts appear in the text layer, image if they appear only in the image.

Figures:
- Report every figure that carries information: screenshots of displays, diagrams, charts, drawings, photos with labels. Skip decorative images, logos and icons that only mark a note or warning.
- `text_in_image`: the labels and text visible in the figure, exactly as shown, that are not in the text layer.
- `values`: every setting, reading or quantity shown in the figure, with its label and unit as shown. Use how = printed for values shown as text. For charts, add a value read off a plotted line only where the chart gives axis scales to read it against, and mark it how = read_from_curve.
- `description`: what the figure shows, in one to three factual sentences. Do not explain, interpret or add knowledge that is not on the page.

OCR:
- Set `ocr_text` to a full transcription of the page only if the text layer is empty or unreadable (scanned page, broken characters). Otherwise set it to null.

Report only what is on the page. If the page has no tables or figures, return empty lists.
